title: Offline Swarm Deployment and Rollout Playbook (VPC & On‑Prem Hybrid)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook documents a validated pattern we call the 'Offline Swarm' — a hybrid private deployment topology for customers that require local inference pods with a lightweight, optionally offline control plane. It covers prerequisites, reference topology, operator-driven rollout steps (canary -> ramp -> full), safe upgrade and rollback procedures for stateful model artifacts and KV caches, post-deployment acceptance tests, and required customer readiness checks. Intended audience: private-deploy field engineers, site reliability engineers (SREs), and customer operators.

Goals and constraints
- Goal: deploy/upgrade inference capacity into a customer VPC or air-gapped site with zero-customer-data-exfiltration risk and minimal disruption to traffic.
- Constraint: some sites operate with intermittent connectivity to Redwood control plane (heartbeat window >= 1h).
- SLOs: production inference endpoints SHOULD meet customer SLOs: p50 < 40ms (small models), p95 < 200ms (medium models), p95 < 450ms (large models) under normal traffic patterns.

Scope
- Applies to: VPC-hosted private deployments and on-prem airgapped sites using the Redwood lightweight operator.
- Not covered: full multi-region public cloud control-plane deployments (use dedicated operator playbooks instead).

Reference topology (textual diagram)
- Local operator (k8s-operator-lite) on management plane (non-privileged)
- Inference pod group(s) (model-runtime) per tenant, with local KV cache and ephemeral model shard store
- Local telemetry forwarder with buffered store-and-forward to central telemetry gateway (optional)
- Optional on-site artifact registry / airgap bundle server (signed images and model weights)

Requirements: customer readiness checklist
| Category | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control connectivity | Periodic outbound TLS to redwood-control.redwood.ai:443 (heartbeat) OR operator in fully-offline mode | Allowlist for artifact fetch from operator only |
| Hardware | 2 x inference GPUs per tenant-class, 64GB system RAM, 2x 10Gb NIC | NVMe local cache, 4+ GPUs for medium/large models |
| Storage | 500GB ephemeral model store | 2TB with snapshotting for high-throughput deployments |
| KMS / key boundary | Customer KMS (AES-256) available for config secrets | HSM integration for signed image attestation |
| Network | VPC subnet with egress control, private peering for telemetry | BGP path for cross-site fallback |

Important notes:
- If site is fully airgapped, follow the airgapped-bundle recipe (see "Artifact bundle & attestation" section) and schedule operator handshake windows for manual attestations.

Artifact bundle & attestation
- Build signed bundles locally or provide signed model artifacts through our secure transfer template. Each bundle MUST include: model sha256, quantization profile tag, runtime-compatibility manifest (v2), and an operator-manifest.yaml with desired model-weight placement strategy.
- Signing: use customer key (recommended) or Redwood-signed attestation when under managed contract.

Operator configuration matrix (example)
| Config key | Example value | Notes |
| operator.mode | offline | offline | 
| operator.heartbeat_interval | 15m | Pulls control intents when available |
| operator.model_prefetch | 2 | Number of model weights to pre-warm per node |
| operator.kv_eviction_seconds | 3600 | Keep prefix caches warm for 1h |
| runtime.max_live_requests | 200 | Per-GPU soft limit |

Pre-deployment validation steps (run by field engineer)
1) Verify customer network egress/allowlist: curl --head https://redwood-control.redwood.ai/health or validate offline mode.
2) Validate hardware inventory: lspci | grep -i nvidia; check NVMe SMART for > 1M IO cycles remaining.
3) Confirm signed bundle integrity: sha256sum model.tar.gz && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature model.tar.gz.sig model.tar.gz.
4) Run smoke container: docker run --rm --read-only --network=host redwood/runtime-check:stable sh -c 'redwood-health --check-kv --check-gpu'

Rollout procedure (operator-driven, recommended cadence)
- Roles: field-engineer (executes operator commands), operator (customer operator), SRE-on-call (Redwood on-call for escalation).
- Canary (T+0): Deploy operator-mode=offline or connected to control plane in read-only. Push model bundle to 1 node:
  1. put operator into maintenance state (operatorctl set-mode canary)
  2. operatorctl apply-bundle --bundle ./signed-bundle.tar.gz --target nodes=node-01
  3. Monitor: runtime/latency p50/p95, kv/hit-rate, GPU temperature. Accept if p95 within 20% of baseline and no OOMs for 10m.
- Shadow traffic (T+1h): mirror 10% of live traffic to canary pod for 2 hours. Required checks: correctness score vs eval prompt set >= baseline - 0.02 absolute.
- Gradual ramp (T+6h): increase traffic in steps: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows at each step.
- Full enroll: when ramp steps pass acceptance gates, mark deployment stable and schedule post-deploy snapshot.

Acceptance gates (automated)
- Perf gate: p95 latency delta <= +25% vs baseline OR absolute p95 under model-class SLOs.
- Quality gate: automated evals on 200 prompt-set samples: mean quality metric delta <= 0.015.
- Resource gate: no GPU mem exceedance > 90% for more than 2 consecutive 1-minute intervals.

Backout & rollback cookbook
- Immediate rollback (triggered by operator or SRE): operatorctl rollback --to-previous --preserve-kv=true. This performs an atomic model pointer switch; model weights are not removed to speed rolling back.
- For stateful KV inconsistencies: follow the KV reconciliation procedure:
  1. Quiesce writes (operatorctl quiesce-tenant <tenant>)
  2. Snapshot current KV: operatorctl kv snapshot --out kv-snap-<ts>.tar.gz
  3. Reconcile by replaying prefetched prefixes from snapshot to nodes marked healthy.
- Evidence preservation: collect /var/log/redwood/operator.log, model load traces, GPU telemetry (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv), and a TLS packet capture (if allowed) for the timeframe of the incident.

Upgrade choreography for model runtime and kernel bundles
1) Preflight: operatorctl validate-runtime-bundle --bundle runtime-bundle.tgz (checks kernel ABI, cuDNN, and kernel selectors).
2) Canary roll: upgrade operator on 1 node, run two inference passes with canary model, validate correctness.
3) Staged roll: waves of 3 nodes with 10–15 minute soak per wave.
4) Post-upgrade: run KV validation job (operatorctl kv-validate --threshold 0.999).

Special case: offline-only sites (no outbound connectivity)
- Use signed-artifact USB / airgapped bundle transfer. All operator commands MUST be executed locally by a customer operator. Redwood provides a signed manifest and verification tool (redwood-offline-verify).
- Scheduled manual attestations: field engineer and customer operator must co-validate bundle checksum and signature. Record attestations in ticket system (include signed manifest).

Monitoring & observability contract
- Local metrics to collect (minimum): runtime.request.latency p50/p95, runtime.kv.hit_rate, node.gpu.utilization, node.gpu.temperature, model.load.time.
- Local retention: minimum 7 days granular metrics; aggregated rollups for 90 days. For airgapped sites, use buffered forwarder to central telemetry when connectivity resumes.

Operator runbook excerpts (quick commands)
- Apply bundle: operatorctl apply-bundle --bundle /opt/artifacts/signed-bundle.tar.gz --target node-02
- Force rollback: operatorctl rollback --to-previous --reason "regression-detected"
- Quiesce tenant writes: operatorctl quiesce-tenant tenant-42

Post-deploy acceptance tests (automated):
- run-eval-runbook --prompts=canary-200.json --baseline-id=canary-baseline-2025 --assert-quality-delta 0.02
- perf-check --rps 20 --duration 300 --assert-p95 < 1.25*baseline

Ownership and escalation
- Deployment owner: eng-private-deployments field-delivery (oncall rota: field-eng@redwood.ai).
- Escalation to SRE oncall if any of the following for > 15 min: sustained p95 > SLO, two or more node OOMs, KV corruption detected.

Runbook appendix: artifact verification examples
> Verify signature:
> openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature signed-bundle.tar.gz.sig signed-bundle.tar.gz

> Check GPU status (example):
> nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used,temperature.gpu --format=csv
